newsitem.title: FRANCE: Australia, France bury nuclear test hatchet.
newsitem.headline: Australia, France bury nuclear test hatchet.

text.p: Australia formally buried the hatchet with France on Monday over Paris' bitterly contested South Pacific nuclear tests when visiting Defence Minister Ian McLachlan announced the restoration of defence ties.

"I am pleased to announce today that the Australian government has appointed a new defence attache to France. This position has been vacant since the recall of the previous defence attache in July 1995," he said in a statement issued as he met French Defence Minister Charles Million in Paris.
Canberra withdrew its military envoy in protest at President Jacques Chirac's decision in June 1995 to resume underground nuclear weapons tests at Mururoa Atoll in French Polynesia.
After a huge international campaign spearheaded by Australia and New Zealand, the tests were concluded ahead of schedule in January. France has since committed itself to a total worldwide test ban.

"A few strands in our relationship were loosened over the testing issue. These have now been pulled tight. The test issue is one which we all believe now belongs in the past," McLachlan said in the statement.
Officials accompanying him said naval exchange visits between Australia and the French overseas territory of New Caledonia would also resume.
